message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I'm p2 with $1711 and a pink monopoly at hotels. The opponent has $1166 and a light blue monopoly with hotels, plus brown houses and dark blue hotels. Two players are bankrupt.

I've already resolved my landing. I can afford the Park Place hotel but not the Boardwalk. Unmortgaging the railroads or Tennessee Avenue would be negative value. I should avoid trading away Tennessee Avenue or cash, and I won't sell hotels before they're needed.

The next roll from Illinois Avenue lands on B&O Railroad, Atlantic Avenue, Ventnor Avenue, Water Works, and Pennsylvania Avenue. Most of these spaces are mortgaged by the opponent or are non-purchase squares.

I'm on Illinois Avenue, which means I already rolled from Kentucky. No rent is due on my own turn.

The next roll from Illinois lands on Atlantic through Chance, all mortgaged by the opponent. Park Place and Boardwalk are 13 and 15 spaces away, so they are not hit this turn. I still need $289 to buy the Boardwalk hotel.

I will reach the dark blue hotels before passing GO. I can afford the Park Place hotel but not the Boardwalk. I am considering selling a pink hotel now to build a cushion.

Selling a hotel returns only half its cost, roughly $50. That is too small to cover the missing Boardwalk hotel. I will keep both pink hotels.

A full pink strip with one house is worth $300, covering the $289 shortfall for Boardwalk. I will keep both hotels and sell reactively if needed. The opponent's next roll from Oriental Avenue lands on Vermont through States, so they cannot collect rent from my properties.

The opponent can land on my pink hotels next turn. From Oriental Avenue, rolls of 5, 7, or 8 reach St. Charles, States, and Virginia respectively. That is a 41.7% chance. Each hotel would cost $750 to $900 in rent. The opponent has $1166.

One pink hotel hit is fully payable from cash alone. A second hit would leave the opponent with only $416, which is enough to cover another $750 but not a $900 hit. Liquidating light blue hotels and brown houses would raise about $425, giving roughly $841 total, which could cover a second $750 rent but still falls short of $900.

The opponent can fully cover a single pink hotel hit from cash alone. They would only need to downgrade dark blue hotels if they land on two pinks in one turn.

Unmortgaging the railroads is negative value. The rent would be only $25, and the unmortgage cost would reduce cash for the Boardwalk. Tennessee Avenue is also unwise because the opponent already holds St. James, New York, and Illinois.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is useless because the opponent does not hold the orange set. Selling a pink hotel would only return about $50, and four houses still charge high rent. The standard rent schedule for St. Charles, States, and Virginia is being reviewed.

Downgrading a hotel to four houses would only return about fifty dollars and still leave the opponent able to pay the reduced rent. A full strip of one house is worth two hundred fifty dollars, which is still short of the two hundred eighty-nine dollar shortfall for Boardwalk. Selling a hotel would also eliminate the seven hundred fifty dollar rent threat.

Trading with the opponent seems unlikely to help. They will not give up their dark blue hotels or light blue monopolies for cash. I do hold Tennessee Avenue, which completes their orange set.

Trading Tennessee Avenue would let the opponent build orange hotels, which are extremely dangerous. Cash trades would only help them unmortgage dormant sets. I have two Get Out of Jail Free cards while they have none, but they have nothing I want to trade for them.
